LESSON: WOOD

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.1: Wood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Wood, part of Materials for Production in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why is wood an important material in day- to–day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to wood as a material of production,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify wood according to physical characteristics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the preparation of wood for use in the production of items,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate types of wood to their uses in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. value the importance of wood in the day-to-day life. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to watch signed/captioned videos or observe a demonstration on how to sign terms related to wood as a material of production. ● In purposive groups, learners practise how to fingerspell and sin terms related to wood as a material of production. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print or digital media to search for information on physical characteristics of wood, discuss and present to plenary. Ensure the discussions are based on bi lingual communication to suit both Hard of Hearing and Deaf learners. Adopt a proper seating arrangement preferably a horse type to allow learners maximum interaction. Also, provide Why is wood an important material in day- to–day life? 25 learners with guiding questions to moderate the discussion. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print or digital media to search for information on the types of wood used at the workplace. ● In pairs, learners are guided to sort wood into either softwood or hardwood. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print or digital media to search for information on how to prepare wood for use in the workplace. ● Adopting a proper seating arrangement, learners are guided to discuss and present their findings on how to prepare wood for use in the workplace. Ensure the discussions are based on bi lingual communication to suit both Hard of Hearing and Deaf learners. Also, provide learners with guiding questions to moderate the discussion. 26 ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss methods of wood preparation for use in the workplace (conversion and seasonin

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. . Provide learners with guiding questions to moderate the discussion. ● Learners are guided to write summary notes on methods of wood preparation for use in the workplace. Ensure learners are provided with supplementary notes on methods of wood preparation for use in the workplace. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print or digital media to search for information on uses of wood in the workplace, discuss and present their findings on uses of wood in the workplace. ● Learners are guided to write summary notes on uses of wood in the workplace. Ensure learners are provided with supplementary notes on uses of wood in the workplace. 27 ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to visit a nearby workplace to explore the uses of wood. Ensure the learners who are deaf are provided with sign language interpretation during the visit. Learners can also interact with the resource persons or the community through written questions and gestures. Learners who are Hard of hearing should be provided with assistive hearing aids which can aid help them interact with the community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Wood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to search for

information on types of wood.

• Learning to learn: learner organises own learning when searching for information on the types of wood used in the

immediate environment.

Values:
• Unity: learner cooperates with others when sharing print or digital media to search for information on types of wood.

• Respect: learner accepts diverse opinions when discussing methods of wood preparation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCI’s):

28

Peer education and Mentorship: interpersonal relationships is enhanced as learner discusses methods of wood preparation for

use in the immediate environment

Links to other Learning Areas:
Social Studies: learner enhances knowledge of resource exploitation as they brainstorm on the uses of wood in different

trades.

Suggested learning resources

• Assorted Pieces of wood (hard and soft)

• Career brochures, career magazines

• Digital devices such as; computer, laptop, smart phone, tablets among others
